newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- US July CPI rises 0.2 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- US July CPI rises 0.2 pct in July.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department said the consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in July against a 0.1 percent increase in June. The core index, which excludes food and energy, was also up 0.2 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.2 percent rise in overall CPI and a 0.2 percent jump on the core.
PHILIP BRAVERMAN, ECONOMIST, DKB SECURITIES: "What we have here is a very low inflation rate."
"Yesterday's (PPI) report showed outright deflation in the pipeline and now we have a confirmation that in the consumer prices we continue to see very subdued inflation."

MATTHEW ALEXY, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, CREDIT SUISSE FIRST BOSTON CORP: "Everything in the report is very close to expectations. There is nothing ugly that we see in the data. So we are fine on the inflation front. The claims figures are about where you would have thought they would be."

DAVID KELLY, SENIOR ECONOMIST, PRIMARK DECISION ECONOMICS: "These numbers were about as expected. The encouraging thing here is that services inflation seems to be still relatively well under control. Overall services were up 0.3 percent, but medical care services were only up 0.1 percent -- that's a pretty good reading.
"We're still waiting for inflation. Year-over-year, we're at 2.2 percent on CPI. That's a very low, very positive number."

ANTHONY CHAN, ECONOMIST, BANC ONE: "The numbers are in line with expectations. The energy price component was no major surprise. The surprise was new cars because these numbers are not giving any indication that prices are accelerating or decelerating.
"These numbers are telling us there is no near-term inflation. Medical care prices really stabilized and that is somewhat favorable.

"The potentially damaging component is food and that was up 0.3 percent. The issue is that food prices have been declining and now they are snapping back. Food prices may not be supportive in keeping prices down in the future. It depends on the weather and what happens to commodities."

DAVID SLOAN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, I.D.E.A.: "The July CPI offered no surprises at all. It just continues the same subdued trend we've been seeing. There was a rebound in airline fares. But that's a volatile component that was soft in June and bounced back in July. When you have a 0.1 percent increase in a month, as we did in June, you often have a 0.3 percent CPI increase the next month. But to have a 0.1 percent rise in June and a 0.2 percent increase in July presents a pretty subdued inflation picture."
